Central Nervous System
Anatomy
Face

Quick Overview

This lesson covers the muscles of facial expression (orbicularis oculi, orbicularis oris, buccinator, platysma), the sensory supply of the face by the trigeminal nerve, the motor supply by the facial nerve and its branches, and facial palsy. It then covers the arterial supply, venous drainage, the dangerous area of the face and lymphatic drainage.

Complete Lesson Content

Muscles of facial expression

Orbicularis oculi (three parts)

PartOriginInsertionAction
OrbitalFrontal process of maxilla; fibres loop around the orbital margin and return to originSkin of eyelids above its originCloses the eye tightly (e.g. intense light)
PalpebralMedial palpebral ligamentLateral palpebral ligamentCloses lids gently (sleep, blinking)
LacrimalPosterior lacrimal crest and lacrimal fasciaUpper and lower eyelid tarsi (mostly lateral palpebral raphe)Dilates lacrimal sac, aiding drainage of tears

Orbicularis oris

Surrounds the oral orifice and forms most of the lips.

  • Extrinsic portion: major bulk; interlacing fibres of surrounding muscles inserted into the lips at the modiolus, most from buccinator.
  • Intrinsic portion: origin by incisive and mental slips from maxilla and mandible near the midline; passes laterally into the lips and interlaces with the peripheral fibres near the modiolus. Narrows the mouth to the smallest circle (whistling).

Buccinator

  • Origin: alveolar margins of maxilla and mandible opposite the three molars, and the pterygomandibular raphe (fibrous band from pterygoid hamulus to posterior end of mylohyoid line, palpable between the posterior ends of the jaws).
  • Insertion: upper fibres to upper lip, lower fibres to lower lip; intermediate fibres decussate (upper to lower lip, lower to upper lip).
  • Actions: compresses cheeks against gums to push food into the oral cavity proper, empties blown-up cheeks, suckling.

Platysma

Origin: skin and fascia of infra- and supraclavicular regions. Insertion: lower border of mandible, skin of buccal region, lower lip. Action: depresses mandible and angle of mouth; tenses skin of lower face and anterior neck.

Sensory nerve supply

The skin of the face is supplied by the trigeminal nerve, except a small area over the ramus of the mandible near the angle, supplied by the great auricular nerve (C2, 3; cervical plexus).

  • Ophthalmic (V1): upper third of face, forehead, scalp up to the vertex.
  • Maxillary (V2): middle third, maxillary sinus, upper lip, upper teeth.
  • Mandibular (V3): lower third, lower lip, lower teeth, part of auricle, anterior part of temporal fossa.

Motor nerve supply: facial nerve (extracranial part)

  • Exits via the stylomastoid foramen, passes forwards lateral to the styloid process, and enters the parotid gland through its posteromedial surface.
  • Before the gland: posterior auricular nerve (scalp behind auricle) and nerve to posterior belly of digastric and stylohyoid.
  • Within the gland: five terminal branches (temporal, zygomatic, buccal [upper and lower], mandibular, cervical) leaving via its upper end, lower end and anterior border.

Facial (Bell's) palsy: paralysis of orbicularis oculi (cannot close the eye, no blinking); frontal belly (loss of forehead corrugations); buccinator (food collects in the vestibule, angle of mouth deviates to the healthy side, cannot blow the cheek); orbicularis oris (cannot whistle).

Blood supply

Besides the superficial temporal, ophthalmic and maxillary branches, the face is mainly supplied by the facial artery.

  • Arises from the external carotid; runs along the posterior border of the submandibular gland deep to the base of the mandible, then between the gland and its fossa to the lower border of the mandible.
  • Hooks around the mandibular base at the lower anterior border of masseter (pulse palpable), runs tortuously up and medially to the angle of the mouth, ascends beside the nose and ends as the angular artery at the medial angle of the eye, anastomosing with ophthalmic branches.
  • Neck branches: submental, ascending palatine, tonsillar, glandular. Facial branches: inferior labial, superior labial, nasal, angular.

Venous drainage

  • Supratrochlear and supraorbital veins unite near the medial angle of the eye to form the anterior facial vein.
  • Superficial temporal vein enters the parotid and unites with the maxillary vein to form the retromandibular vein, which divides into anterior and posterior divisions leaving through the gland's lower end.
  • Anterior division + anterior facial vein form the common facial vein, ending in the internal jugular vein.
  • Posterior division + posterior auricular vein form the external jugular vein.
  • Occipital vein (back of scalp) ends in the suboccipital venous plexus.

Dangerous area of the face

Triangle between the root of the nose and the lateral angles of the mouth. It connects to the cavernous sinus by two routes:

  • Long ophthalmic veins: supratrochlear and supraorbital veins directly to the cavernous sinus.
  • Deep facial vein: anterior facial vein to pterygoid venous plexus, which connects to the cavernous sinus by emissary veins.

Lymphatic drainage

RegionNodes
Central lower lip, chinSubmental
Anterior scalp, lateral lower lip, upper lip, medial cheek, foreheadSubmandibular
Sides of scalp, lateral faceParotid (then submandibular)
Posterior scalpPosterior auricular and occipital

Efferents of all these nodes end in the upper deep cervical nodes.

Key Points / Quick Review

Muscles

  • Orbicularis oculi: orbital (tight closure), palpebral (gentle), lacrimal (dilates sac).
  • Buccinator: pterygomandibular raphe origin; decussating intermediate fibres.
  • Platysma depresses mandible and mouth angle.

Nerves

  • Sensory: V1, V2, V3; great auricular (C2, 3) over mandibular angle.
  • Motor: facial nerve; five terminal branches inside the parotid.
  • Bell's palsy: no eye closure, no forehead wrinkles, no whistling, mouth deviated to healthy side.

Vessels and lymph

  • Facial artery ends as angular artery.
  • Retromandibular vein divides; common facial vein to IJV, external jugular from posterior division.
  • Dangerous area drains to the cavernous sinus via ophthalmic and deep facial veins.
  • Chin/central lower lip: submental nodes.
